exchanges.question: How does Lilly see the consumer/self-pay obesity market evolving (including aesthetic-driven approaches), and how similar is the U.S. self-pay market to the international one?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Obesity treatment utilization is still mid-single-digit in the U.S. and globally; access is improving with Bridge and some state Medicaid programs going live or committing to next year, obesity TRxs are around 3 million, and about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions are self-pay; Lilly is investing in consumer awareness and expanding LillyDirect. Jonsson: outside the U.S. obesity is still mainly out of pocket; Lilly is replicating U.S. consumer practices and has launched versions of LillyDirect OUS, but models will differ because regulations differ.

exchanges.question: Why has the U.S. Foundayo launch curve been slower than anticipated and when will it inflect; and how are OUS competitive dynamics shaping up as Novo scales its oral pill, including Novo's claim of 50% UAE share within three weeks?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Focus is on physician education, access/affordability and consumer awareness; CVS added Foundayo in June, Bridge launched July 1 and full DTC began; in the last week of July volume was almost doubling versus a month ago and around one in four new starts is on Foundayo, which Yuffa called an inflection point. Jonsson: UAE launched early May with a strong start, most patients incretin-naive, and Lilly's combined incretin share held steady despite a second oral; Mexico and Saudi launch next, most launches in 2027, with no supply gating; early data is noisy and often sell-in reflecting inventory build.

exchanges.question: What are the requirements and milestones for retatrutide to be accepted as a BLA, and would that classification be unique to retatrutide or extend to subsequent incretins?
exchanges.answer: Lilly believes retatrutide is a biologic under the amino acid count rule and as analogous to a protein; the first court decision was mixed and litigation is active, and Lilly hopes to reach a conclusion with FDA supporting a BLA. All clinical data needed to submit is in hand but more CMC data must be gathered; Lilly is in communication with the agency and will update investors on filing status. Submission expected by Q1 next year; Ricks cited a large lead over any triple-acting competitor.

exchanges.question: What are the early learnings and ramp from the Medicare obesity (GLP-1 Bridge) rollout, and how are orals versus injectables tracking?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Bridge increases obesity-therapy access by about 35% more Americans; it is early but showing a significant inflection, with prior authorization working and criteria clear, and LillyDirect enabled to fulfill Bridge. ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO both inflected over the last few weeks, partly from Bridge; around 80% of patients are on injectables, and an estimated 60%-70% are new patients who had no access before.

exchanges.question: Does retatrutide need a commercial strategy against unauthorized versions available today or will approval solve it; and does its higher efficacy open indications beyond tirzepatide's?
exchanges.answer: People are awaiting authentic retatrutide and are expected to 'vote with their feet' once it is approved. Higher efficacy opens new opportunities: knee osteoarthritis pain reduced by 75% in TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1; a MASH/MASLD study is ongoing where glucagon action may be unique; a chronic lower back pain study reads out sometime next year; several further indications are being evaluated internally.

exchanges.question: What is the post-Verzenio breast cancer strategy given the oral SERD and oral PI3K, and is an all-oral combination planned?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: The key breast cancer targets are ER, CDK4/6 and PI3K alpha; Lilly believes it has the best medicine for each and plans to combine them all. EMBER-4 adjuvant trial for imlunestrant (INLURIYO) reads out next year; the tersolisib (PI3K inhibitor) phase III is about to begin, initially with existing endocrine therapies plus investigator's-choice CDK4/6 (largely Verzenio), later combining with INLURIYO, enabling an all-oral combination.

exchanges.question: Guidance seems to imply H2 revenue deceleration versus Q2 despite Bridge and Foundayo access; is something on price being missed or is it conservatism?
exchanges.answer: The full-year guide was raised by $2.5 billion; prior-period adjustments to U.S. rebate and discount estimates (including this quarter) are not expected to continue in H2. The H2 2025 base included the bolus of MOUNJARO launches in new countries, which will not recur, so percentage growth slows though dollar growth stays significant and future OUS growth comes from penetration. Europe Q3 seasonality and U.S. Type 2 diabetes Q4 seasonality are factored into the guide.

exchanges.question: Which regions are driving OUS MOUNJARO growth, and what is happening in India with generic semaglutide launches and reported capacity constraints?
exchanges.answer: MOUNJARO holds market leadership across many markets; China NRDL achieved category leadership after 16 months, with significant growth in Korea, the U.K., Mexico and Germany, and share in many markets similar to or above the U.S. In India and Brazil MOUNJARO TRx kept growing after generic semaglutide launched, attributed to superiority data; in Canada tirzepatide TRx grew at the same pace as the total market; generic makers are seeing significant supply constraints.

exchanges.question: How extensive is Foundayo sampling and is it dampening IQVIA prescription data; and can Lilly quantify expansion of the U.S. prescriber base?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Sampling covers the first 30 days of the first dose, typical for a retail oral small molecule, extensive across prescribers and fully supplied. Prescribers rose to 36,000 from 8,000 cited on the last earnings call, with week-on-week progress; the effect of sampling on IQVIA data was not addressed directly.

exchanges.question: ZEPBOUND net price is about $580 per prescription, above cash price; how sustainable are medical exceptions now CVS is back on formulary, and are they behind the recurring favorable rebate adjustments?
exchanges.answer: Pricing is transparent: LillyDirect $299 to $449 and Bridge $245, plus commercial; script size also drives the per-prescription figure, so price per pack is significantly lower. CVS access starting in Q4 will reduce medical exceptions, which are a short-term thing; Lilly expects price to go down, which is embedded in guidance, and to more than offset it with volume growth.

exchanges.question: Are psychiatry and vaccines areas Lilly can scale as a priority, or are the deals one-offs driven by the science?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Both areas share immense unmet need, the through line of internal and BD work; assets were bought at prices that keep Lilly disciplined and create long-term value, similar to other deals year to date. He declined to forward look on building further in infectious disease or psychiatry, saying Lilly will be opportunistic based on what is available.

exchanges.question: Which one or two non-obesity pipeline assets should the Street pay more attention to?
exchanges.answer: Cardiovascular: PCSK9 gene editing plus oral and injectable Lp(a)-lowering drugs; neuroscience: psychiatry, sleep-wake via Centessa, and addiction and major depressive disorder possibly via incretin science; oncology is probably the richest readout period in Lilly's history, highlighting Kelonia's in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma and AJ1-11095 JAK inhibitor. Immunology: growth of the drug transcribed as 'empagliflozin' with new indications, plus combinations in IBD and psoriatic diseases; he called it the strongest pipeline Lilly has ever had even excluding incretins.

exchanges.question: Given Foundayo UAE sales of $31 million versus $67 million in the U.S. (analyst figures), what is the ex-U.S. obesity potential; and will ex-U.S. governments reimburse Foundayo for diabetes better than tirzepatide given a lower price?
exchanges.answer: Encouraged by UAE but it is very early, data is noisy and includes initial inventory build; most patients are incretin-naive, showing need for an oral in obesity and Type 2 diabetes. Major OUS rollout happens at the beginning of 2027. Lilly is probably slightly better positioned for Type 2 reimbursement with an oral and three head-to-head trials, but OUS reimbursement always takes time, so launch focus will be chronic weight management.
